_README: Slots for the CROSS-LINGUAL probe: the question is asked IN each language, not only
in French, so each language gets its own prompt and its own next-token distribution.
WHY THE PREFIX IS NO LONGER DECLARED. token_probes.json had to name, per slot, the
French answer prefix to truncate at, because one French distribution was read five
ways. Here each language is prompted separately, so the truncation point is simply
'just before this language's own spelling of the answer' -- the script derives it by
finding the target inside that language's gold answer. One thing to declare instead of
two, and it cannot drift out of sync with the data.
TARGETS ARE CANDIDATE LISTS, tried in order, first match wins. The published ja/id/ru
translations were not inspected when this file was written, so each entry carries the
plausible spellings. The script prints every gold answer it loads and names any slot
where no candidate matched, so one run is enough to correct the misses -- a wrong guess
costs that one cell, never the job.
A target must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the answer, or the truncation point is ambiguous
and the script skips the cell rather than guessing which occurrence was meant.
role=primary  the answer is a COMMON noun, translated differently in all five: the
model must retrieve the concept and express it in the prompt language.
role=contrast the answer is a PROPER noun, carried across languages as the same string
(or a transliteration): it tests whether the memorised SURFACE FORM
transferred, not whether the fact did. Reported beside the primary slots
because the two coming apart is the finding -- a name that transfers
while an occupation does not means transfer is lexical, not semantic.
DROPPED: f2_birth_city. The question contains 'al-Kuwaits' and the answer is Kuwait, so
base Qwen3 already ranks ' Kuwait' FIRST at p=0.137 with no training at all. That slot
measures copying from the prompt, not knowledge.
